entries.title: Shikanga v Kenvest Hospitality Kenya Limited (Cause E105 of 2024)
entries.court: Employment and Labour Relations Court of Kenya
entries.principle: Unfair termination requires a valid reason and a fair procedure; the employer bears the burden of proving both.

entries.title: Tips (Kenya) Ltd v Nyaundi (Appeal 2 of 2024)
entries.court: Employment and Labour Relations Court of Kenya
entries.principle: Unfair termination requires a valid reason and a fair procedure; the employer bears the burden of proving both.

entries.title: Joseph Makau Mutava v Kenya Builders Co. Ltd
entries.court: Employment and Labour Relations Court of Kenya
entries.principle: An employer must justify termination on substantive and procedural grounds; unfair termination attracts compensation.

entries.title: Package Insurance Brokers Limited v Gichuru
entries.principle: Indirect discrimination is assessed by identifying the relevant policy or practice, its disparate impact, the disadvantage suffered by the claimant, and whether it is objectively justified and proportionate.
entries.facts: Simon Gitau Gichuru, an operations manager at Package Insurance Brokers Ltd, underwent spinal surgery and was later suspended and dismissed, allegedly due to his disability and medical condition.
entries.holding: The Court of Appeal found that his dismissal amounted to indirect discrimination and was unfair because the employer failed to accommodate his condition and provide a fair hearing. It partly allowed his appeal and awarded compensation.
entries.judges: PN Waki, MS Asike-Makhandia and F Sichale JJA

entries.title: Erustus Kambu Mwamburi & Another v Abercrombie & Kent Coast Ltd
entries.court: Employment and Labour Relations Court of Kenya
entries.principle: Unfair termination claims require proof of the employment relationship and the circumstances of termination; the court awards compensation for unfair dismissal.
